title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

constraints.meaning: At least two numbers, so a pair always fits. At most 30,000 numbers.
constraints.impact: Checking every pair is about 4.5 × 10⁸ sums: too slow. One pass, O(n), is the target.
A sum of two values is at most 2000 in size, so int never overflows.

constraints.text: numbers is sorted in non-decreasing order
constraints.meaning: Each value is greater than or equal to the one before it. Equal values can sit next to each other.
constraints.impact: This is the key clue. Moving right to the left can only make the sum smaller; moving left to the right can only make it bigger. So two pointers can steer towards target.

constraints.meaning: target can be negative or zero.
constraints.impact: No special case: the comparison total < target works for any sign.

constraints.meaning: There is always one pair, and only one.
constraints.impact: The loop always finds it, so the code after the loop is never reached. No need to choose between answers.

constraints.meaning: The answer counts positions from 1, not from 0.
constraints.impact: Return [left + 1, right + 1]. left < right holds in the loop, so the order is right.

constraints.meaning: No extra array or hash map.
constraints.impact: Rules out the hash-map answer from Two Sum (LC 1). Two pointers use O(1) space.

bruteForce.summary: check every pair (i, j) with i < j: O(n²) time, O(1) space. A hash map finds the pair in O(n) time, but it needs O(n) extra space, which breaks the constant-space rule.
